I'd probably have a few of yours on my list if I hadn't played them to death. Most middle-years Pink Floyd was basically on a permanent loop in my room. I can barely sit through it without twitching. This is an odd list that probably changes daily, but whatever:

  1. Marvin Gaye - What's Goin On? Great voice, great soul, great album.

  2. Kiss - Destroyer. Kiss wasn't allowed in my house when I was growing up, so I had to go down the street to my friend's house to listen to it. I found this album at just the right time, and so it sticks with me completely. Except for 'Great Expectations.' That song blows.

  3. Slayer - Reign in Blood. Every track is perfect. Even the track order is perfect. Don't have any coffee in the house? Put this on and you're awake.

  4. Gordon Lightfoot - Sit Down Young Stranger. 70s folk music does it for me, and the lyrics and breadth of subject matter make it always interesting. Masterful lyrics.

  5. Tarkio - Brewer & Shipley. I like every song on this album. Mellow, casual, and perfect for sitting on the porch and drinking beers.

Meddle - Pink Floyd. Honestly as an album the songs hold together than most of their other albums (which are mind blowing by themselves). I just think if you're going to listen to a whole album, that one is the best

Spectra - Chipzel. It's a great way to get someone into chiptunes. This is the chick who made the music for Super Hexagon, and the album is put together beautifully. Its my favorite work by her

Out of the Blue - Electric Light Orchestra (ELO). Honestly this is just one I like for nostalgia, plus the songs are boppy and fun to listen to. It flows well and is just an enjoyable album

Monument - Royksopp and Robyn. Probably my favorite recent album to come out, its very fun and some good synth and a pairing up of two great artists.

Cure for Pain - Morphine for those muddy, dirty, grungy blues days. Although I love all their albums, I do have a soft spot in my heart for this one.
